 ERW Steel Pipe Supply and Selection 
 Forever Steel supplies electric resistance welded (ERW) steel pipe for projects that permit the specified welded route. Select the governing standard, grade and service requirements first, then confirm OD, wall thickness or schedule, length, weld-seam inspection, coating and release documents. 
 Use the 
SCH 40 and SCH 80 pipe dimensions chart
 to check nominal wall thickness. A schedule is not a pressure rating or a guarantee of ERW availability. Where the specification requires a seamless route, see 
seamless steel pipe options
. 
Compare manufacturing routes before RFQ:
 use the 
ERW, seamless, LSAW and SSAW pipe decision guide
 to check service, size and wall range, weld inspection, availability and project approval before fixing the ERW route. 
 1. Technical Specifications & Size Range 
 Outside Diameter (O.D.): 1/2" – 26" (21.3mm – 660mm) 
 Wall Thickness (W.T.): Confirm the exact OD/wall combination against the governing standard and quotation. Schedule availability varies by diameter and grade. 
 Pipe Length: 5.8-12 m; confirm the ordered length, tolerance and any custom-length requirement in the quotation.

integration into global supply chains:

 3. Pipe End Preparation 
 To ensure efficient on-site installation, we offer professional end 
finishing: 
 Bevelled Ends:Standard 30° (+5°/-0°) with 1.6mm root 
face (per ANSI B16.25) for easy welding. 
 Plain Ends:Square cut for structural use or socket 
welding. 
 Threaded & Coupled (T&C):Precise threading according to API 5B or ASTM standards. 
 Grooved Ends:Suitable for rapid mechanical coupling 
systems. 
 4. Surface Treatment & Corrosion Protection 
 Customized coating solutions to protect against atmospheric and 
soil corrosion: 
 Temporary Protection:Black Varnish 
painting or Light Oiling. 
 High-Durability Coating:Hot-Dipped Galvanized (HDG) – Zinc coating up to 500g/m². 
 Advanced Anti-Corrosion: 3PE (Three-Layer Polyethylene), FBE (Fusion Bonded Epoxy), or 3PP coating for 
underground burial. 
 5. Packaging & Logistics Excellence 
 We understand that long-distance international shipping requires 
superior packaging to prevent damage: 
 Hexagonal Bundling:Small diameter pipes 
are bundled with high-tensile steel strips and heavy-duty nylon lifting slings. 
 End Protection:Heavy-duty plastic caps or metal ring 
protectors to safeguard bevels and threads. 
 Sea-Worthy Marking:Each pipe is 
stenciled with Heat No., Size, Grade, Standard, and Manufacturer Logo(Customized marking supported). 
 Loading Precautions: 
 Use of wooden dunnage and rubber separators to prevent 
steel-on-steel friction. 
 Rigid bracing and lashing within containers or bulk vessels to 
prevent shifting during transit. 
 6. Quality Assurance (QA/QC) 
 Mill Test Certificate (MTC):Issued according to EN 10204 3.1 or 3.2. 
 Third-Party Inspection:We 
welcome and facilitate inspections by SGS, BV, TUV, or Lloyd's Register. 
 Testing Protocol: Hydrostatic testing, weld-seam UT/ET or other NDT, and flattening/bending tests are performed when required by the governing standard, purchase order and approved inspection and test plan (ITP). 
 7. ERW Manufacturing Route and Purchase Decision Guide 
 ERW pipe should be selected by service, governing standard, weld-seam requirements and the feasible OD/wall-thickness combination—not by price or diameter alone. Confirm whether the purchase specification calls for ERW, HFW or another welded route, because terminology and acceptance requirements vary by standard and edition. 
Project need
When ERW may fit
Evidence to confirm before order
 API 5L line pipe 
 Efficient production for compatible line-pipe sizes and grades when the project accepts the specified ERW/HFW route. 
 API 5L edition, PSL, grade, product specification level, service conditions, toughness/NDT clauses and approved manufacturing procedure. 
 Water, gas or general pressure service 
 Commonly considered where ASTM A53, EN 10217 or another applicable pressure-pipe standard permits electric-welded pipe. 
 Exact standard and grade, design pressure/temperature, hydrotest requirement, end preparation, coating/lining and regulatory approvals. 
 Structural tube or piling 
 Suitable when dimensional consistency, production length and project economics are important. 
 Structural standard, section/pipe designation, OD, nominal and design wall thickness, straightness, end condition, weld acceptance and load basis. 
 Heavy wall, severe service or restricted route 
 Compare seamless, LSAW or another approved route rather than assuming ERW is interchangeable. 
 Route feasibility, sour/low-temperature service, CVN/HIC/SSC requirements when specified, wall-thickness capability and owner approval. 
Weld-seam and traceability evidence
 Coil or strip identity linked to the finished pipe and material test certificate. 
 Forming, welding and weld heat-treatment records where required by the governing specification or approved procedure. 
 Weld-seam UT, ET or other NDT method, coverage, calibration standard and acceptance result as required by the standard, purchase order and ITP. 
 Hydrostatic, flattening, bend, tensile, dimensional and visual inspection records when applicable to the ordered product. 
 Pipe marking, heat/coil/pipe traceability, MTC, NDT report, hydrotest record and third-party release when specified. 
RFQ fields for comparable ERW quotations
Define in the RFQ
Why it matters
 Standard and edition; grade; PSL or delivery condition where applicable 
 Prevents quotations based on different technical baselines. 
 ERW/HFW route; OD; wall thickness or schedule; length and quantity 
 Confirms the exact size-route combination and production feasibility. 
 Service medium; design conditions; low-temperature, sour or other supplementary requirements 
 Triggers the necessary material, toughness, corrosion and inspection review. 
 Ends, coating/lining, cutback, marking, packing and delivery terms 
 Aligns fabrication and shipment scope before price comparison. 
 Hydrotest/NDT scope, MTC type, inspection documents and third-party witness points 
 Makes acceptance evidence part of the order rather than an assumption after production. 
Published ranges are quotation starting points. Final availability and acceptance depend on the exact standard edition, grade, dimensions, service conditions and approved inspection plan.
 8. Strategic Application Sectors 
 ERW steel pipes are 
engineered to deliver reliability across diverse and demanding environments: 
a. Energy & 
Hydrocarbon Infrastructure
 A primary solution for 
the gathering and transmission of crude oil, natural gas, and refined 
petroleum. ERW pipes are highly valued in the energy sector for their balance 
of high tensile strength and economic viability. 
b. Public Utilities 
& Water Management
 Essential for 
large-scale municipal water supply systems, irrigation networks, and sewage 
treatment facilities. Their compatibility with various anti-corrosion linings 
ensures a long service life in underground environments. 
c. Structural 
Engineering & Construction
 Extensively utilized in 
the construction of airports, stadiums, and high-rise buildings as structural 
hollow sections (HSS). They offer excellent load-bearing capabilities for 
piling, trusses, and decorative architectural frameworks. 
d. Industrial & 
Fire Safety Systems
 The industry standard 
for fire-protection sprinkler systems and low-pressure steam/air conveyance. 
Their durability ensures system integrity during critical emergency responses. 
e. Mechanical & 
Automotive Manufacturing
 High-precision ERW 
tubes are vital components in the automotive industry (chassis and steering 
columns) and the manufacturing of heavy-duty machinery, rollers, and conveyor 
systems.

ERW Pipe Production Process
 ERW steel pipe is produced from steel coil through strip preparation, continuous roll forming and electric resistance welding of the longitudinal seam. The pipe then passes through finishing and inspection stages before marking, packing and dispatch. The sequence below outlines a typical high-frequency ERW route; heat treatment, testing and surface protection depend on the specified standard, grade and purchase requirements. 
 ERW Production Steps and Quality Controls 
1. Coil Inspection and Strip Preparation:
 Check coil identification, material records, thickness, width and surface condition against the order. Uncoil and level the strip; prepare its edges for consistent forming and weld fit-up. 
2. Strip Joining and Accumulation:
 Join successive strip ends and use an accumulator to support continuous feeding. These strip-end joints are distinct from the finished pipe's longitudinal seam and require control under the applicable production procedure. 
3. Roll Forming:
 A series of rolls progressively shapes the strip into an open tube. Control edge alignment and forming geometry before the strip reaches the welding station. 
4. High-Frequency ERW Welding and Bead Removal:
 High-frequency current heats the strip edges, which are pressed together to form the longitudinal seam. Remove the external and, where specified and accessible, internal weld bead to the required profile. 
5. Heat Treatment and Cooling:
 Apply seam heat treatment or other specified treatment according to the product standard, grade and approved manufacturing route. The diagram's post-annealing stage does not mean every ERW order receives the same annealing treatment. 
6. Sizing, Cutting and End Preparation:
 Size the pipe to control diameter and roundness, cut to the ordered length and finish the ends. Confirm whether the order requires plain ends, bevels or another agreed preparation. 
7. Inspection and Testing:
 Check dimensions and surface condition. Perform weld-seam NDT, hydrostatic testing and required material tests to the applicable standard and inspection plan; specify methods, coverage and acceptance criteria for the order. 
8. Surface Protection, Marking and Dispatch:
 Apply the ordered coating or temporary protection. Verify identification and traceability, protect the ends as required, and prepare packing and loading arrangements for the agreed transport method. 
Before ordering:
 Confirm the standard and edition, grade, OD and wall thickness, length, heat-treatment requirements, NDT and pressure-test scope, end finish, coating and required inspection documents. 
Frequently Asked Questions
1. How do you guarantee the weld quality of ERW steel pipe before shipment?
We implement internal quality control from raw material review to final shipment release. For orders related to water lines, structural applications, scaffolding, and medium-diameter pipeline projects, buyers usually expect the product to match both the application and the supporting ERW steel pipe, ASTM A53, API 5L ERW pipe, and UT inspection on the weld seam requirements.
2. Do you provide UT records, hydro test results, and MTC for ERW steel pipe?
Yes. We can provide Mill Test Certificates according to EN 10204 3.1, and 3.2 can be arranged when required. Third-party inspection by agencies such as SGS, BV, or ABS can also be accepted before shipment.
3. How do you protect ERW pipe ends and bevels during truck transport and sea freight?
We use export-oriented packing and loading methods based on the product type, including end protection, stable bundling or blocking, waterproof wrapping where needed, and careful loading control. The goal is to reduce rust, scratches, bevel damage, face damage, coating damage, thread damage, or handling impact during domestic transport and long sea shipment.
4. Is ERW steel pipe normally used for water lines and structural steel applications?
This product is commonly supplied for water lines, structural applications, scaffolding, and medium-diameter pipeline projects, with buyer demand often tied to ERW steel pipe, ASTM A53, API 5L ERW pipe, and UT inspection on the weld seam.
